While the basic premise—a working-class woman marrying into a wealthy family with an intimidating matriarch—is a familiar setup in fiction, the story actively subverts the cliches associated with this trope. Instead of being a cruel, classist villain who looks down on the protagonist's background, Miss Emily deeply respects Nell's work ethic and discipline as a cashier. Furthermore, rather than abandoning her old life for a glamorous makeover or taking a high-powered job at her mother-in-law's company, Nell finds her identity and pride by returning to her $11-an-hour supermarket job on Saturdays. The prose is also fresh and relies on unique, specific observations rather than overused expressions.
